newsitem.title: POLAND: EU's Brittan urges Poland to resolve trade rows.
newsitem.headline: EU's Brittan urges Poland to resolve trade rows.

text.p: European Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan warned Poland on Thursday not to spoil its preparations for EU entry by failing to settle trade disputes with the bloc over issues such as duty-free imports of Korean car parts.

Brittan told a business forum in Warsaw that Poland was a major partner and future member of the Union, highly praising its economy and its preparations to join the EU including its newly-issued Strategy for National Integration.
But he said there were unresolved issues.

"I am particularily thinking of the favourable treatment provided by the Polish authorities to the Korean car manufacturer Daewoo and the obligatory certification system imposed on a number of EU products...," he said.

"The impression is given that a number of separate initiatives have been taken in Poland to provide unjustified protection to domestic producers and domestic production facilities," he told the Polish Business Roundtable.

"After all that has been achieved, we must not allow such issues to interrupt the further development of our political and economic relations, and to give ammunition to those who wish to cast doubt on them," Brittan, a strong backer of Polish EU entry, said in a speech issued in advance to reporters.
Poland hopes to begin talks on EU entry early next year, once the union's 15 members complete their inter-governmental conference, and is trying to adjust its laws to get ready.

But the EU is indignant that Daewoo is allowed to import car kits duty-free for easy assembly at the former FSO car plant it acquired in Warsaw last year, saying this gives an Asian rival a back-door entry into Europe.
Brittan said some Poland-EU quarrels, notably over Warsaw's attempts to prolong protection of its oil and steel sectors, were near an interim solution after talks last year.
"The details of these deals are still to be confirmed and implemented in full and it is, of course, essential that this should happen as soon as possible," Brittan said.
His visit also follows the European Commission's launch in December of anti-dumping proceedings against Polish zinc producers -- a charge disputed by the Polish companies.
Brittan applauded Poland's improved offer during World Trade Organisation talks on deregulating telecommunications.
"However, the impact of the Polish offer would be even greater if it was more generous on the treatment of foreign investment," Brittan added.

Poland is gradually liberalising its domestic telecommunications market and preparing to privatise the current state monopolist Telekomunikacja Polska SA, but plans to keep restrictions on foreign operators for some time.

Brittan met President Aleksander Kwasniewski after arriving on Thursday and said later that he had mentioned the various difficulties in Polish-EU relations and would discuss them in more depth with ministers during his two-day trip.
Kwasniewski's aide Marek Siwiec told a news conference after the meeting that Poland also had some complaints over access by its goods to the EU, with which it runs a deficit.
"There are conflicts -- and the will to resolve them," Siwiec said.
During Brittan's visit EU and Polish teams are to hold two days of technical talks on a range of issues.
